executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
The Westin Grand München appeared in at least one AI answer for 65.1% of the traveler needs we tested, showing that AI recognizes the hotel as relevant across a broad range of stays. Across every individual AI answer, however, The Westin Grand München appeared 49% of the time. In practical terms, the hotel fits many of the searches being made, but a traveler will not consistently see The Westin Grand München in the hotel options surfaced.

The clearest strength in this period is often placed near the top when ai ranks hotels. See the summary at left for the supporting numbers. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, The Westin Grand München appeared in the Top 3 80% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

The main opportunity is consistency: the hotel is already relevant across many traveler needs, so the next focus is understanding where it is absent from individual AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: The Westin Grand München's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers.
sections.keyInsight: Family-Friendly is recognized in only 6.5% of monitored answers. That is low enough to matter commercially if the attribute is part of how the hotel should win relevant traveler needs. Overall scores can hide this concentrated representation miss. Broader Scenario Presence (65.1%) and Consideration (49%) do not, by themselves, prove the distinctive attribute is traveling into answers.
sections.whyItMatters: If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on Family-Friendly. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.
sections.whatToReview: Open Reality Gap evidence for Family-Friendly and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named.
